metadata.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX's Nvidia-powered orbital data center could be ready next year

content.text:
SpaceX (SPCX) launched 29 Starlink satellites this week. CEO Elon Musk also noted that the company's first Nvidia-powered (NVDA) orbital data center could launch in the fourth quarter of 2027.
Yahoo Finance Breaking Business News Reporter Jake Conley chats with Yahoo Finance Senior Autos Reporter Pras Subramanian and Business Insider executive editor and anchor Dan DeFrancesco about what's next for the company.
We saw a launch of some more Starling satellites, uh, like last night over into the morning today. But the big news today coming out, SpaceX saying its first Nvidia powered orbital data center could launch in the fourth quarter of 2027 with scale coming in 28. The question to me just keeps being, is this an actual economically feasible business?
Right, I mean, they basically moved up a timeline just a little bit, right?
Right, it's like from 2028.
early to end of 2027.
Right, we're moving it up just a little bit.
And it's like, well, Elon Musk, the guy loves aggressive timelines. It's as a goal post and who knows if they'll hit. Stock isn't really moving that much on this, right? So it's just a little tweak there but it's, I guess a good thing to hear if you're a SpaceX investor. This is becoming more and more a reality. Uh, when when we first started talking about orbital data centers, we were like, are you kidding me? This seems this sounds impossible.
This is a hundred years from now.
It sounds like an insane science fiction. And then you start hearing more and more about it. It's like, okay, that could work. Okay, that could work. Oh they got Starlink there to connect for connectivity. That could work. Uh you don't cooling's not necessarily an issue. Okay. Unlimited power if you're facing the sun. Okay, fine. So it makes more and more sense. I'm just concerned about a timeline that is this student and you still have Starship which is necessary for this type of a a launch not yet fully there yet. and it's happening slowly. So, I think you got to see more with Starship, right? before you start talking about putting these massive orbital data centers up in space, in my opinion.
Yeah.
I mean, does anybody love pushing up a timeline more than Elon Musk?
No.
Like, it's just, you know, uh death taxes and Elon saying he's going to do something faster than initially he said.
Guy sleeps on the factory floor.
I know all the employees got just a pit in their stomach.
Right, right. Oh, no, dude, he did it again. Oh, no.
But the counter is like, you know, 10 years ago if you said, oh, we're going to build rockets that are going to be able to self land like you'd be like, no, there's no way. And then he did it. So like ultimately, in the long run, right, short term is different, but in the long run, betting against Elon Musk is a losing endeavor for anyone who's ever basically did it. So, um, as aggressive as this timeline does and is there maybe a little bit of like, oh, we'll pump up the timeline, you know, we're below the IPO price, blah, blah, blah, you know, now we'll try to get a boost here. Maybe, you know, there's a little bit of of that to try to kind of appeal to investors, but um it's it's tough to count him out to do anything because he's proven time and again he's been able to to nail it a lot.
Is it also interesting that this is all coming out right right ahead of Nvidia earnings?
That's right. Two big Nvidia pieces, you know, tied to Musk, tied to SpaceX. Find that timing a little interesting. But it also kind of leads credence to oh they're Nvidia powered data centers? Oh, that's interesting. Oh, that's that sounds sounds legit to me.
Right.
